2. The petitioner instituted Other Suit No. 650 of 1978 on 13.6.1978 in the court of Munsif Sadar Mymensingh, against the opposite party No. 1 and another for declaration of title in respect of 0.15 acres of land appertaining to plot No. 2263 of CS Khatian No. 171/199 and ROR Khatian No. 1 of mouza Fulbaria on the allegations inter alia, that the petitioner was the owner of the said land but in the last ROR operation the said land was, wrongly recorded in khatian No. 1 in the name of the government as khas land. The opposite party No. 1 claimed title in thy said land on the basis of settlement which created cloud over the title of the petitioner. The opposite party No. 1 and the petitioner on 10.9.1982 filed a petition of compromise in the said suit and the opposite party No. 1 admitted the title of the petitioner. Sub-sequent, the opposite party No. 1 on 16.2.1983 filed an application for not recording compromise on the basis of the said compromise petition. The petitioner objected to the said application. The learned Munsif, however on 10.4.1983 rejected the compromise petition leading to filing Miscellaneous Appeal No. 82 of 1983 in the court of District Judge, Mymensingh. The said appeal and the suit are pending before the courts for disposal. 

 5. Next, she submits that the learned Munsif committed an error in law in holding that the claims in the two suits are different and upon such erroneous view wrongly rejected the application. She submits that in an application under section 10 CPC the relief sought for is immaterial either for allowing or rejecting the application. She submits that the subject matter in issue is material and not the claim of the parties. She further submits that the learned Munsif also committed an error to say that the relief’s claimed in the two suits are not same. She contends that in the earlier suit filed by the petitioner the relief sought for was that the petitioner is the owner of the land in suit and preparation of the record of rights in the name of the Government under khas khatian was wrong. In the subsequent suit also the relief sought for was that the Government is the owner of the land. Therefore, she submits that in both the suits the subject matter relates to ownership of the land in suit which requires adjudication by the courts. From the record it seems to me that the contention of the learned Advocate has substance. In aid of her submission she cites the decision in the case of Sakhawat Hossain Vs. Chowdhury Muhammad Sarwar and others, PLD 1968 Dac 557 wherein it has been held that the difference in the relief claimed in the two suits is quite immaterial under section 10 of the Code. A careful examination of the provision of section 10 CPC seems to me that the matter in issue in the previously instituted suit and in the subsequent suit is material consideration for the court in an application under section 10 CPC and not the relief sought for in the said suits. The case of Sakhawat Hossain also supports this view of mine. Accordingly; I set aside the impugned order and allow the application filed by the petitioner under section 10 CPC and direct to stay the trial of the Title Suit No. 92 of 1983 pending in the court of Upazila Munsif, Fulbaria, District Mymensingh.
